name: pwm_controller
description: Parameterized PWM controller with synchronous active-low reset. The counter increments on each rising clock edge while enable is asserted, rolls over to zero when it reaches the programmed period, and pwm_out is a combinational compare of counter_value against duty_cycle. All state initializes to zero on reset_n low.

fixed_assumptions: period[7:0] is treated as an inclusive terminal count for rollover; when enable is high and counter_value equals period, the next clocked value becomes zero.
duty_cycle[7:0] and period[7:0] are sampled combinationally for pwm_out and for rollover comparison.
pwm_out is purely combinational from counter_value and duty_cycle and is not separately registered.

feature_contracts.description: Asserting reset_n low clears the observable counter state and forces the design into its reset baseline.
With reset released and enable asserted, the counter advances on each clock until rollover conditions apply.
With reset released and enable deasserted, the counter holds its current value and pwm_out remains the combinational compare of that held value against duty_cycle.
pwm_out reflects counter_value < duty_cycle as a combinational compare.
When enable is high and the counter reaches the programmed period, the next counted state rolls over to zero.

functionality: Implements a programmable pulse-width modulation generator. The internal counter advances by one on each active clock edge when enable is high, resets synchronously to zero when reset_n is low, and wraps to zero when the counter reaches the programmed period value. The PWM output is asserted whenever the current counter_value is numerically less than duty_cycle. The module exposes the current counter_value for observability and downstream integration.
responsibilities: Generate a periodic count sequence under enable control.
Provide a duty-cycle-based PWM output derived from the current count.
Support synchronous active-low reset of all registers to zero.
Expose the current counter value as an output for monitoring and system use.
reset_behavior: When reset_n is low, the counter register is synchronously cleared to zero on the next rising edge of clk, and the externally visible counter_value shall be zero. Because pwm_out is combinational from counter_value and duty_cycle, it evaluates low during reset when counter_value is zero and duty_cycle is not less than zero; with the specified reset baseline and zeroed registers, pwm_out is low after reset until the counter and duty inputs create a true compare condition.
behavior_rules: On each rising edge of clk, if reset_n is low, set counter_value to 8'h00.
On each rising edge of clk, if reset_n is high and enable is low, hold counter_value at its present value.
On each rising edge of clk, if reset_n is high and enable is high, increment counter_value by one unless the present counter_value is equal to period, in which case load zero on the next state.
The comparison for rollover is based on the current registered counter_value versus period; the counter wraps after reaching the terminal count.
pwm_out shall be high whenever counter_value < duty_cycle, otherwise low.
counter_value is a direct observable representation of the registered count state.
No internal memory macros are used in this design.
